payload.name: ExtractPreferenceFromPositiveExclamations
payload.description: When extracting candidates, if a speaker expresses a positive evaluation or exclamation about an object, place, or experience (e.g., 'X is so beautiful!'), create a durable preference memory for that speaker toward the evaluated thing.
content: During candidate extraction, treat explicit positive evaluative exclamations (e.g., 'so beautiful', 'love it', 'amazing') as evidence of the speaker's durable preference.
Create a `preference` candidate linking the speaker to the object of evaluation only when the statement expresses the speaker's own judgment, not a reported or hypothetical opinion.
Extract at most one preference per distinct evaluated object per message; stop once the preference is captured to avoid redundant candidates.

solves: Construction extraction fails to generate any candidate when a speaker states a durable preference as an exclamatory positive evaluation (e.g., 'The autumn colors are so beautiful!'), leaving the fact absent from memory. This applies to future sessions where a speaker makes an explicit first-person aesthetic or positive evaluation of an object, place, or experience. It does not apply to reported opinions of others, transient states, or explicit 'I like' statements that the base extraction policy already handles.
